newsitem.title: UK: LCE coffee recovers after slide to 4-week lows - Sept 6.
newsitem.headline: LCE coffee recovers after slide to 4-week lows - Sept 6.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures pared some losses after bargain-hunting on Friday to end above new four-week lows of $1,520 a tonne hit earlier on trade and fund selling, traders said.
"There is still risk of further downside potential but we saw good industry and roaster support as prices slid," said one.
Chart-driven and fundamental selling on Friday combined forces to whack prices down to a fresh four week-lows of $1,520 a tonne basis November. The contract closed $28 lower at $1,534.
Technical selling was triggered as prices sliced through key support at $1,550 a tonne on Friday, while hedge selling against a volume of 445 lots on November puts also helped, said traders.
"There was good system and options-related selling," said one.
Put options on November were most active at a strike of $1,550 a tonne.

On the fundamental side, expectations for higher supply in the 1996/97 period and reports that an Italian court has ruled compensation be meted out to companies who ten-years-ago suffered huge losses from a price boosting operation - the so-called Patricia Operation - also weighed on sentiment.
If the ruling is upheld, the Brazilian government could be transferring some 338,739 60-kg bags of coffee, held for years in a Trieste warehouse, to four or five companies.
"It could be a factor. The threat of the Patricia coffee has been in the market for some time," said one.
"It is quite a bit of coffee...And it won't help prices when released," said another London-based dealer.
Total volume on the exchange reached 6,331 lots at the close on Friday.
